basis: Bounded follow-up source review completed at 2026-10-05 20:23:48 UTC for the full 11-root scorecard. Review began at 20:23:08 UTC. Retrieval/review times remain separate from source publication dates and market observation times.

ISM September 2026 Services PMI was scheduled today at 14:00 UTC and the official report body is available. It is post-release background, not a future catalyst or fresh directional market observation.
Official ISM page HTML title says September 2025, while its visible heading, table and history say September 2026. Record this source-metadata conflict; do not silently substitute a different year.

At the 20:23 UTC follow-up, accessible primary Fed H.15 and H.10 snapshots still identify October 2 and September 28 releases, with observations through October 1 and September 25 respectively. The scheduled October 5 20:15 UTC publication time has passed, but updated publication is not verified through these retrieved pages. A cached/lagging page cannot establish that the publisher has not released new data. No eligible current nominal/real-yield or dollar observation was obtained.
No long/short alignment numbers are invented from qualitative narrative. Every root has null alignment and UNKNOWN evidence; missing evidence earns zero rather than neutral credit.

Future calendar entries are schedule context, not numeric trade direction. Calendar review is partial, and no absence-of-risk or CLEAR conclusion is made. No event-blackout window or veto policy is configured.
Publication timestamps remain null where the primary source does not disclose a precise publication time. Scheduled times are not relabeled as actual publication or market-observation times.
CME session schedules are informational. Contract-specific differences must be preserved, especially the two-minute weekday crypto maintenance period; this file creates no session-trading veto.

The EIA outlook schedule page returned HTTP 503 on this review. Its accessible main page reconfirms October 6 as the next release date. The noon–12:15 ET normal publication window remains from the successful 19:49 review, not a newly fetched timing observation.
No fresh directional geopolitical or market-response evidence was verified during this bounded follow-up. ISM and OPEC source event dates are unchanged; their retrieval does not renew their age.
